newsitem.title: USA: Valero sets East Texas pipeline expansion.
newsitem.headline: Valero sets East Texas pipeline expansion.

text.p: Valero Natural Gas Corp said Wednesday it plans to substantially expand the capacity in its East Texas natural gas pipeline that runs from Bethel in Anderson County, to the Carthage hub in Panola County.

The Valero Energy Corp subsidiary said the expansion is expected to take place in three phases over the next 18 to 24 months and will add some 465 million cubic feet per day of capacity to the present 400 million cubic feet daily at a cost of $11.7 million.
Valero said the expanded capacity will support the growing Pinnacle Reef reserves being developed in the area.

"With this expansion, Valero will provide natural gas producers and gatherers operating in the Pinnacle Reef area with additional transportation capacity and access to our Carthage hub and the higher-valued markets in the East.

"We have recently signed long-term agreements with Sonat Inc subsidiaries and Delhi Gas Pipeline for capacity in our East Texas pipeline and we are discussing similar arrangements with other parties who have interests in this rapidly developing play," Valero said.

Nearly a month ago the USX-Delhi Group said new facilities had added 100 million cubic feet per day of natural gas gathering and treating capacity to the 60 million built in late 1995. At the time, spokesman Mike Dixon said Phase II will add 275 million cubic feet of daily capacity.

About a week later, Western Gas Resources Inc announced plans for a 200 million cubic feet per day natural gas processing plant in East Texas and a 45 mile pipeline from the plant to the Pinnacle Reef play.
With the exception of measurement, Valero said, virtually all of the expansion will be accomplished by installing additional compression on the pipeline.
